newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Milburn still awaits Chinese cement price lift.
newsitem.headline: Milburn still awaits Chinese cement price lift.

text.p: New Zealand cement company Milburn Ltd said on Monday a lift in cement prices in China to more realistic levels was not expected for some time.
Milburn operates the Golden Cat Cement Works in Suzhou, 100 km from Shanghai.

"In China, a gradual relaxation of government monetary controls as inflation is brought under control should assist the Golden Cat Cement Works, although a lift in cement prices to more realistic levels is not expected for some time," Milburn said.
Earlier, Milburn reported a NZ$49.9 million operating profit for 1996 excluding its Chinese investments and a total net operating profit of $24.3 million for the year.
Milburn said building activity in China was depressed during 1996.

"Financial restraints introduced by the authorities were successful in lowering inflation but as a consequence of the tight credit controls there was a weaker demand for cement, severe price competition in the oversupplied Shanghai market, and liquidity problems amongst construction companies," it said.
It said these factors had an adverse affect on Golden Cat Cement's sales revenue, trading results and debtor collections.
However progress was made in identifying areas for efficiency gains, it added.
